```{python}
#| output: false
import glob
import sys
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import xgboost as xgb
from pathlib import Path
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_point, geom_line, geom_col, geom_abline, geom_jitter,
    labs, theme_minimal, coord_flip, scale_color_manual,
)
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import HTML, display

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "nhl" / "pbp" / "parquet").is_dir():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "python"))
from nhl_data_build import xg_train as xt

files = sorted(glob.glob(str(ROOT / "nhl" / "pbp" / "parquet" / "play_by_play_*.parquet")))
pbp = pl.concat([pl.read_parquet(f) for f in files], how="diagonal_relaxed")
boosters = {}
for v in ("5v5", "st"):
    b = xgb.Booster()
    b.load_model(str(ROOT / "models" / f"xg_model_{v}.json"))
    boosters[v] = b

def gt_show(g):
    display(HTML(g.as_raw_html()))
```

The fastRhockey xG suite estimates the probability that an unblocked shot
becomes a goal, in two strength regimes: **5v5** (all non-shootout,
non-penalty-shot unblocked shots) and **special teams** (power play /
short-handed). A third component, the **penalty-shot constant**, is the
historical conversion rate computed at train time. The suite's output ships
as the xG columns inside every published `nhl_pbp_full` season asset — the
model never ships alone; it reaches consumers embedded in the play-by-play.

The models are XGBoost binary classifiers (logloss objective), a faithful
reproduction lineage of the hockeyR xG recipe (Morse 2022), re-fit on this
repository's own committed corpus by `python/nhl_data_build/xg_train.py`
(canonical R twin `R/build_xg_model.R`). The fitted boosters are **committed
in this repo** (`models/xg_model_{5v5,st}.json`) — that is the promotion step
— and every figure and number below is computed at render time from those
committed artifacts plus the committed play-by-play.

## Training data

```{python}
seasons_tbl = (
    pbp.filter(pl.col("event_type").is_in(xt._FENWICK))
    .group_by("season").agg(
        pl.col("game_id").n_unique().alias("games"),
        pl.len().alias("fenwick_events"),
        (pl.col("event_type") == "GOAL").mean().alias("goal_share"),
    ).sort("season")
)
gt_show(
    GT(seasons_tbl.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Committed NHL play-by-play corpus, by season",
                subtitle="unblocked shot events (SHOT / MISSED_SHOT / GOAL); computed at render time")
    .fmt_number(columns=["fenwick_events"], sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_percent(columns="goal_share", decimals=1)
)
```

Training corpus: this repository's committed play-by-play
(`nhl/pbp/parquet/`, seasons listed above, ~13.6M events). Seasons are
grouped into **five era buckets** (2011–2013, 2014–2018, 2019–2021,
2022–2024, 2025-on) that enter as one-hot features, so rule- and
tracking-era shifts are modeled rather than silently biasing the fit. The
5v5/ST split is a modeling decision, not a convenience: shooting talent and
shot-quality distributions differ enough across strength states that a single
pooled model miscalibrates the power play.

## Exploratory data analysis

```{python}
#| output: false
frames = {}
rng = np.random.default_rng(37)
splits = {}
for v in ("5v5", "st"):
    fr = xt.prepare_training_frame(pbp, variant=v)
    frames[v] = fr
    tr, te = xt._grouped_split(fr, rng)
    _ = rng.permutation(tr["game_id"].unique().to_list())  # replay the fold draw
    splits[v] = (tr, te)
f5 = frames["5v5"]
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Goal rate by shot distance, 5v5 model frame — the dominant feature."
d = (
    f5.with_columns((pl.col("shot_distance") / 5).floor().alias("bin"))
    .group_by("bin").agg(pl.col("goal").mean().alias("goal_rate"),
                          pl.len().alias("n"), pl.col("shot_distance").mean().alias("dist"))
    .filter((pl.col("n") >= 500) & (pl.col("dist") <= 90)).sort("dist")
)
(
    ggplot(d.to_pandas(), aes("dist", "goal_rate"))
    + geom_point(aes(size="n"), color="#2a6f97", alpha=0.8) + geom_line(color="#2a6f97")
    + labs(x="shot distance (ft)", y="observed goal rate",
           title="NHL goal rate by shot distance (5v5 frame)")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
shot_mix = (
    f5.select([c for c in xt._SHOT_TYPE_COL.values() if c in f5.columns] + ["goal"])
    .unpivot(index="goal", variable_name="shot_type", value_name="is_type")
    .filter(pl.col("is_type") == 1)
    .group_by("shot_type").agg(pl.len().alias("shots"), pl.col("goal").mean().alias("goal_rate"))
    .sort("shots", descending=True)
)
gt_show(
    GT(shot_mix.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Shot-type mix and conversion (5v5 frame)")
    .fmt_number(columns="shots", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_percent(columns="goal_rate", decimals=1)
)
```

Distance dominates conversion — from ~25% at the crease to ~2% beyond 60 ft —
and the shot-type table explains the one-hot block: tips and deflections
convert well above wrist shots from similar range, and the model needs the
type to separate them. The special-teams frame adds `total_skaters_on` and
`event_team_advantage`, the two features that encode the man-advantage state.

## Feature importance

```{python}
imp_rows = []
for v, b in boosters.items():
    for f, g in b.get_score(importance_type="gain").items():
        imp_rows.append({"variant": v, "feature": f, "gain": float(g)})
imp = pl.DataFrame(imp_rows)
top5 = imp.filter(pl.col("variant") == "5v5").sort("gain", descending=True).head(12)
topst = imp.filter(pl.col("variant") == "st").sort("gain", descending=True).head(12)
gt_show(
    GT(top5.rename({"gain": "gain_5v5"}).drop("variant").to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Top 12 features by gain — 5v5 booster (committed artifact)")
    .fmt_number(columns="gain_5v5", decimals=1)
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Gain importance, both committed boosters (top 12 each)."
both = pl.concat([top5, topst]).to_pandas()
(
    ggplot(both, aes("reorder(feature, gain)", "gain", fill="variant"))
    + geom_col(position="dodge")
    + coord_flip()
    + labs(x="", y="gain", title="xG feature importance (gain)")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

## SHAP

TreeSHAP attributions come directly from the committed boosters
(`pred_contribs=True` — exact for tree ensembles, no extra dependency). The
distribution of per-shot attributions for the top features shows how each
one moves individual shots on the log-odds scale:

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "TreeSHAP per-shot attributions, 5v5 booster, top 8 features by mean |SHAP|; 4,000-shot sample."
b5 = boosters["5v5"]
feats5 = b5.feature_names
rs = np.random.default_rng(11)
samp_idx = rs.choice(f5.height, size=min(4000, f5.height), replace=False)
Xs = f5.select(feats5).to_numpy().astype(float)[samp_idx]
contribs = b5.predict(xgb.DMatrix(Xs, feature_names=feats5), pred_contribs=True)[:, :-1]
mean_abs = np.abs(contribs).mean(axis=0)
order = np.argsort(mean_abs)[::-1][:8]
rows = []
for j in order:
    for i in range(Xs.shape[0]):
        rows.append({"feature": feats5[j], "shap": float(contribs[i, j])})
shap_df = pl.DataFrame(rows).to_pandas()
(
    ggplot(shap_df, aes("feature", "shap"))
    + geom_jitter(width=0.25, alpha=0.05, size=0.4, color="#2a6f97")
    + coord_flip()
    + labs(x="", y="SHAP (log-odds)", title="TreeSHAP attributions per shot — 5v5")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
shap_tbl = pl.DataFrame({
    "feature": [feats5[j] for j in order],
    "mean_abs_shap": [float(mean_abs[j]) for j in order],
})
gt_show(
    GT(shap_tbl.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Mean |SHAP| — 5v5 booster, 4,000-shot sample")
    .fmt_number(columns="mean_abs_shap", decimals=4)
)
```

## Evaluation

Two views, honestly labeled. First, the **frozen training-time gates**: the
grouped 5-fold CV metrics observed at the 2026-04 fit, below which a retrain
fails (`--quick` smoke runs tolerate misses; a real retrain does not):

| variant | CV AUC (observed at fit) | CV log-loss | frozen floor |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5v5 | **0.8322** | 0.2053 | cv AUC ≥ 0.82 |
| special teams | **0.8213** | 0.2567 | cv AUC ≥ 0.81 |

Second, a **reproduced grouped split evaluated at render time**: the same
seed-37, game-grouped 80/20 partition recipe the trainer uses, applied to
*today's* committed corpus, scoring the committed boosters on the 20% side.
Because the corpus has grown since the fit (new games, repairs), this is a
*near*-holdout — some evaluation games were in the boosters' training data —
so read it as a stability check on live data, not a pristine test score.

```{python}
rows = []
for v in ("5v5", "st"):
    tr, te = splits[v]
    b = boosters[v]
    X = te.select(b.feature_names).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = te["goal"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    p = b.predict(xgb.DMatrix(X, feature_names=b.feature_names))
    base = float(tr["goal"].mean())
    rows.append({
        "variant": v, "eval_shots": te.height, "goal_rate": float(y.mean()),
        "logloss": xt._logloss(y, p),
        "baseline_logloss": xt._logloss(y, np.full_like(p, base)),
        "rank_AUC": xt._rank_auc(p, y),
    })
ev = pl.DataFrame(rows)
gt_show(
    GT(ev.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Reproduced grouped-split evaluation (render-time, current corpus)",
                subtitle="seed-37 game-grouped 80/20 recipe; committed boosters scored on the 20% side")
    .fmt_number(columns="eval_shots", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
    .fmt_percent(columns="goal_rate", decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(columns=["logloss", "baseline_logloss", "rank_AUC"], decimals=4)
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Calibration by xG decile, 5v5, reproduced-split evaluation shots."
tr5, te5 = splits["5v5"]
b5 = boosters["5v5"]
p5 = b5.predict(xgb.DMatrix(te5.select(feats5).to_numpy().astype(float), feature_names=feats5))
dec = (
    pl.DataFrame({"xg": p5, "goal": te5["goal"].to_numpy().astype(float)})
    .with_columns((pl.col("xg").rank("ordinal") * 10 / pl.len()).ceil().clip(1, 10).alias("decile"))
    .group_by("decile").agg(pl.col("xg").mean(), pl.col("goal").mean(), pl.len().alias("n"))
    .sort("decile")
)
(
    ggplot(dec.to_pandas(), aes("xg", "goal"))
    + geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="gray")
    + geom_point(aes(size="n"), color="#2a6f97") + geom_line(color="#2a6f97")
    + labs(x="mean predicted xG (decile)", y="observed goal rate",
           title="5v5 calibration — reproduced split")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Per-era discrimination: rank AUC of the committed 5v5 booster by era bucket (evaluation shots)."
era_cols = [c for c in feats5 if c.startswith("era_")]
te5e = te5.with_columns(pl.Series("xg", p5))
era_rows = []
for ec in era_cols:
    sub = te5e.filter(pl.col(ec) == 1)
    if sub.height < 5000:
        continue
    era_rows.append({"era": ec.removeprefix("era_"),
                     "AUC": xt._rank_auc(sub["xg"].to_numpy(), sub["goal"].to_numpy().astype(float)),
                     "n": sub.height})
era_df = pl.DataFrame(era_rows).to_pandas()
(
    ggplot(era_df, aes("era", "AUC", group=1))
    + geom_point(aes(size="n"), color="#2a6f97") + geom_line(color="#2a6f97")
    + labs(x="era bucket", y="rank AUC", title="5v5 xG discrimination by era")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

## Results — players and teams

```{python}
latest = int(pbp["season"].cast(pl.Int64).max())
cur = pbp.filter(pl.col("season").cast(pl.Int64) == latest)
fr_cur = xt.prepare_training_frame(cur, variant="5v5")
shooter = (
    xt._harmonize(cur).with_columns(secondary_type=xt._norm_secondary())
)
# score the current season's 5v5 frame with the committed booster
pcur = boosters["5v5"].predict(
    xgb.DMatrix(fr_cur.select(feats5).to_numpy().astype(float), feature_names=feats5))
# re-attach shooter identity by rebuilding the same filter chain (incl. the
# null-drop set: every nullable feature in prepare_training_frame's keep list
# derives from shot_distance / shot_angle / time_since_last / last_x / last_y)
def frame_with_identity(pbp_in):
    df = xt._harmonize(pbp_in).with_columns(secondary_type=xt._norm_secondary())
    df = df.filter(
        (pl.col("period_type") != "SHOOTOUT")
        & ((pl.col("secondary_type") != "Penalty Shot") | pl.col("secondary_type").is_null())
    )
    grp = "game_id"
    df = df.with_columns(
        last_event_type=pl.col("event_type").shift(1).over(grp),
        time_since_last=pl.col("game_seconds") - pl.col("game_seconds").shift(1).over(grp),
        last_x=pl.col("x").shift(1).over(grp),
        last_y=pl.col("y").shift(1).over(grp),
    )
    df = df.filter(pl.col("event_type").is_in(xt._FENWICK)
                   & pl.col("last_event_type").is_in(xt._VALID_LAST))
    return df.drop_nulls(subset=["shot_distance", "shot_angle", "time_since_last",
                                 "last_x", "last_y"])
ident = frame_with_identity(cur).select(
    "event_player_1_name", "event_player_1_id", "event_team", "event_type")
assert ident.height == fr_cur.height  # same filter chain, row-aligned
scored = ident.with_columns(pl.Series("xg", pcur))
players = (
    scored.group_by("event_player_1_id")
    .agg(pl.col("event_player_1_name").first().alias("player"),
         pl.col("event_team").last().alias("team"),
         pl.len().alias("shots"),
         pl.col("xg").sum().alias("xG"),
         (pl.col("event_type") == "GOAL").sum().alias("goals"))
    .drop_nulls("event_player_1_id")
    .with_columns((pl.col("goals") - pl.col("xG")).alias("GAX"))
    .sort("xG", descending=True).head(15)
    .with_columns(
        ("<img src='https://assets.nhle.com/mugs/nhl/latest/"
         + pl.col("event_player_1_id").cast(pl.Int64).cast(pl.Utf8)
         + ".png' height='42'/>").alias("headshot"))
)
gt_show(
    GT(players.select("headshot", "player", "team", "shots", "xG", "goals", "GAX").to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Top 15 skaters by 5v5 expected goals — season {str(latest)[:4]}-{str(latest)[4:]}",
                subtitle="unblocked 5v5 shots scored by the committed booster; GAX = goals above expected")
    .fmt_markdown(columns="headshot")
    .fmt_number(columns=["xG", "GAX"], decimals=2)
    .cols_label(headshot="", player="Player", team="Team", shots="Shots",
                xG="xG", goals="G", GAX="GAX")
)
```

```{python}
teams = (
    scored.group_by(pl.col("event_team").alias("team"))
    .agg(pl.len().alias("shots"), pl.col("xg").sum().alias("xG_for"),
         (pl.col("event_type") == "GOAL").sum().alias("goals_for"))
    .with_columns((pl.col("goals_for") - pl.col("xG_for")).alias("GAX"))
    .sort("xG_for", descending=True)
)
gt_show(
    GT(teams.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"Team 5v5 shot generation — season {str(latest)[:4]}-{str(latest)[4:]}")
    .fmt_number(columns=["xG_for", "GAX"], decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(columns="shots", sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
)
```

Positive GAX marks finishing above shot quality. At the team level, xG-for
minus goals-for separates shot-generation strength from shooting luck — the
spread between the two is exactly what the embedded xG columns in
`nhl_pbp_full` exist to expose.

## Provenance & reproducibility

- **Trained on:** this repository's committed play-by-play
  (`nhl/pbp/parquet/`, seasons in the corpus table above), 2026-04 fit;
  grouped 80/20 split by `game_id`, grouped 5-fold CV for
  `min_child_weight`, seed 37.
- **Artifacts:** `models/xg_model_5v5.json`, `models/xg_model_st.json`
  (committed — the promotion step); output ships inside `nhl_pbp_full`.
- **Retrain:** `scripts/nhl_models.sh` (stages `nhl_model_01_xg_5v5` /
  `nhl_model_02_xg_st`; fingerprint-skipped when unchanged; gates frozen in
  `models/manifest.yaml`, registry row in `models/REGISTRY.md`).
- **Rebuild this document:** `scripts/render_model_docs.sh` (Quarto → GFM;
  uses this repo's `.venv` via `QUARTO_PYTHON`; `uv sync --group docs`).

## Avenues for improvement & open issues

- **Pre-shot context** — rush/rebound flags exist, but passing sequences and
  screens do not; public-feed models plateau here, so the honest gain is
  better rebound/rush definitions, not more trees.
- **Commit the python meta sidecar** — `xg_model_meta.json` (feature lists +
  per-retrain metrics) is regenerated per run but only the R-era `.rds` is
  committed; committing the json would let this document quote the exact
  training-time holdout metrics instead of the CV gates.
- **Exact holdout reproduction** — the render-time evaluation is a
  near-holdout because the corpus has grown since the fit; persisting the
  training-time game-id partition alongside the meta would make the exact
  test set reproducible forever.
- **Known issue:** the ST sample is ~5× smaller than 5v5 — its gate floor is
  lower for that reason, and per-season ST calibration drift is unmonitored.
